summary.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volumes up 11% YoY, led by double-digit growth in performance surfactants and high single-digit growth in specialty products; non-Tier 1 and direct-to-consumer volumes grew near double digit.

segments.name: Rest of World (Americas, APAC, Europe)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6% YoY; Americas led on tariff clarity and TRI-K premium specialties; APAC grew double-digit. Specialty mix improved, lifting EBITDA/MT.

segments.name: AMET (incl. Egypt)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 4% YoY but up 19% QoQ; about seven weeks of Q1 at the Egypt site were effectively lost because raw materials were stuck at Jebel Ali, Jeddah and Port Said/Suez ports; management called this supply-led, not demand-led.

segments.name: EPC service income (Mexico project)
segments.commentary: Separate business model, not part of performance segment; income recognised in Q1 with amount not disclosed (management said not significant to overall numbers); recognition to complete by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance maintained at 6–8%.
FY27 EBITDA per MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000.
Management indicated INR 21,000–22,000/MT for the next three quarters, implying the INR 35,458 Q1 level is not sustainable.
Fatty alcohol expected to trade sideways at INR 2,600–2,800/MT (ex-Indonesia-type range), with no major expected jumps or corrections.
Annual capex around INR 150–200 crore; management referenced about INR 150 crore for this year.
Specialty products targeted to contribute more than 5% of total revenue by 2030 (per management).
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR 150–200 crore, with some capacity already front-loaded and commissioned; some more to be commissioned this year.
Capacity in place for petrochemical derivative-based products, but supplies were constrained because the derivative was not available; oleochemical use was prioritised.
No acquisition planned in AMET; any AMET capex will be debottlenecking.
Inorganic growth in Beauty and Wellness under evaluation; management hopes to announce something in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Reformulation tailwind: oleochemical-based solutions became more attractive as petrochemical availability and cost worsened after West Asia developments; management expects this to persist for some time.
Feedstock: crude averaged above USD 100/bbl in Q1; oleochemical feedstock ranged USD 2,800 to 3,300/MT, then fell below USD 2,500/MT by late June.
Freight rates on exports more than doubled, feeding into CIF-linked pricing; rupee moved from INR 88 to INR 95 per USD (per management).
Price pass-through: management said customers accept increases when transparently justified; contractual business has a cost pass-through methodology; decreases passed on at the first opportunity.
BASF announced closure of its sulfation plant in Dahej; management said it is too early to quantify any demand upside.
Customer restocking was seen ahead of festive and summer demand, plus some extra buying on fears of feedstock availability; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/kg at INR 35,000 in Q1, and how much came from inventory gains or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reformulation-led volume recovery and operating leverage, specialty mix improvement, and commercial opportunities; some may not persist. It did not quantify inventory gains, but said mix and freight also contributed. Without these, it said EBITDA/MT would have been about INR 21,000.

qa_highlights.question: Is the specialty share decline from about 40% to 34% a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty absolute revenue grew strongly; the share fell because performance products grew faster, enlarging the denominator.

qa_highlights.question: Will AMET return to positive volume growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was supply-led, not demand-led, with Egypt effectively washed out for about seven weeks; sequential growth of 18–19% and June momentum support a recovery, and it sees AMET returning to growth this year absent a new shock.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of reformulation reversing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reformulation remains favourable while petrochemical and oleochemical balance holds; it does not see a big risk currently but will monitor coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 22–23/kg gross margin or INR 25/kg EBITDA a steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the structure has improved but said it wants at least one more quarter before changing long-term guidance, to avoid overpromising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing gain is from finished-goods inventory spikes or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight costs, mix shift toward dry (100%/95% active) products, and the reformulation mix all lifted realisations; it declined to quantify the ASP increase excluding these.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and Indonesia's biodiesel mandate?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is around USD 1,100–1,200/MT and the mandate is largely priced in; fatty alcohol expected to hold at INR 2,600–2,800 on a sideways basis, with El Nino a possible supply-side risk for next year.
